page.layout: One column of running text, with a centred chapter heading "CAPUT V." above the body. No marginal notes. The printed page number and running head are at the top, and the catchword "fit" is at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Resp. Concedo conclusionem de bono essentiali & transcendente, de quo vera est assumptio: non vero de bono accidentali & particulari, ut morali. Sic verus testis, id est, non fictus, non imaginarius, qui verus est essentialiter, potest esse falsus testis, id est, falsum dicere: quod accidentarium est.
main_text.head: CAPUT V.
main_text.p: Hactenus quomodo solvenda sit vitiosa argumentatio, seu fallax ratiocinatiuncula, cum peccatu vel etiam peccatiolum est in materia: Sequitur de ratione solvendi, cum in Forma vitium est.

2. Hic solutio fit Reprehensione [illegible, ~8 letters], id est, consecutiae, quae redargutio, Græcis est [illegible, ~10 letters] & [illegible, ~9 letters]: id est: hic negatur, complexionem e præmissis confici, quod cōsecutio cum legibus syllogisticæ [illegible, ~8 letters] non congruat.
3. Reprehensio consecutionis nonnunquam fit Retorsione ipsius objectionis in opponentem.

p.i: Intellige consecutionem seu consequentiam [illegible, ~10 letters], id est, maximè proprie dictam, hoc est, syllogisticam seu formalem.

page.notes: The Greek words in lines 2 and 3 of the 2nd paragraph and in the italic passage are too small and blurred to read letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. "cōsecutio" has a tilde over the o, which is read as an omitted n. The final "fit" sits alone at the lower right and is taken as a catchword, not as text. The large initial "H" of "Hactenus" is joined to the following word. The page number is printed in old style (looks like "78").
